title: The Lang–Plaut problem
description: OpenAI's negative answer (2026) to the Lang–Plaut problem: a doubling subset of Hilbert space that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional space. The course builds the set from coloured strips at rapidly decreasing scales and proves its doubling bound, differentiates the Lipschitz sheets of a supposed embedding near a lexicographically maximal derivative, proves two energy estimates, and turns crossings of rows and columns into a packing contradiction in Euclidean space.

units.title: Lipschitz sheets and a lexicographic maximum

prerequisites: core course Measure and Integration (Fremlin, Measure Theory: Volume 1, 134A; Volume 2, 225E, 251N, 252B, 252D, 261E, 262B, 262Q, 263A)
core course Real Analysis II (compactness of the unit sphere of R^k, minima of continuous functions)
